Maria (DB): Heads up — planning a schema migration for users.profile to add `preferred_locales` (jsonb) + a staged backfill next Wed 2026-04-01 11:30 UTC. Expect minimal DDL lock (ADD COLUMN). Backfill will run as throttled jobs. Proposing a dual-write window 11:30-12:30 UTC. Who can own the deploy and smoke checks?

Sam (eng-platform): I'm on call that day, I can help with deploy and smoke at 11:25-12:00 UTC. Quick Q: will writes be behind a feature flag during the dual-write?

Maria (DB): Yes — we'll flip `users.preferred_locales_enabled` flag before starting the backfill so app writes populate new column. Reads will fallback to old behavior until rollout finished.

Lee (infra): How heavy is the backfill? ETA? Any risk to replica lag?

Maria (DB): Backfill estimate: ~2M rows, we'll run in batches of 1k via the backfill workers. Throttle target ~200 writes/s, expected ~20-40m for full run but we'll do canary on a 10k slice first. We'll monitor replica lag and pause if > 30s.

Priya (oncall): Rollback plan? If something goes wrong during dual-write, what's the safe step?

Maria (DB): Rollback steps (short):
```sql
-- stop backfill workers
-- disable feature flag so app stops writing to the new column
-- if urgent revert schema change (destructive) only after ensuring column is unused:
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS preferred_locales;
```
But note: dropping the column is last-resort. Preferred rollback is to stop writes and let reads fall back to old logic.

Jen (release-manager): I'll own the deploy. Plan:
- 11:20 UTC: prod deploy (DDL included), feature flag toggled off initially
- 11:25 UTC: run canary backfill on 10k users (monitor errors, latency, replica lag)
- 11:35 UTC: if canary OK, enable dual-write flag and start full backfill throttled
- 12:25 UTC: start verification, disable dual-write after verification

Sam (eng-platform): Smoke checks list I propose:
- 3 sample user profile GETs (uid 101, 202, 303) return expected shape
- POST update profile for sample user succeeds and preferred_locales populated
- No increase in 5xxs or SQL errors in logs
- Replica lag < 30s, DB write latency P95 unchanged (< 120ms)

Priya (oncall): I'll add a pager rule to watch for >0.5% errors over 5m. Also create a quick dashboard with: writes/s, replica lag, backfill job queue depth, failed backfill tasks.

Maria (DB): Canary backfill command (workers):
```bash
# run a single worker job for canary slice
rake backfills:preferred_locales[limit=10000,batch_size=1000,throttle=200]
```
We'll run that at 11:25 and watch.

schema-bot: Migration tracker created: MIG-2026-042, runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/MIG-2026-042. Owner: Jen.

Lee (infra): I'll keep an eye on infra side. If replica lag spikes I'll pause the job and notify.

Sam (eng-platform): I'll prepare a quick rollback playbook in the runbook: commands to disable flag + pause workers + contact points.

Jen (release-manager): Can the team ack availability? I need at least one engineer for rollback tasks in case.

Maria (DB): I'm available 11:00-13:00 UTC.

Sam (eng-platform): Ack, available.

Lee (infra): Ack.

Priya (oncall): Ack and I'll be on-call for alerts.

Jen (release-manager): Perfect. I'll schedule the deploy and post a short status thread in #eng-platform at start and after canary.

Sam (eng-platform): Also tagging @frontend-team to verify client toggles won't break.

FrontendBot: Message sent to #frontend-team: "Heads up: migration and dual-write next Wed 11:30 UTC. Please verify feature-flag handling."

Jen (release-manager): LGTM. :thumbsup:

Maria (DB): Thanks all — I'll add a short checklist to the runbook and link to the migration PR.
